items.title: Section: All-Wisdom, Wondrous Wisdom, and the Grand Closing Statement — All One Hundred Forty Qualities Now Named

items.zh: 當知此中，若諸如來或於能引無義聚法，或於非能引有義聚法非能引無義聚法，總於如是一切法中無顛倒智，是名如來一切種智。若諸如來，於其能引有義聚法一切法中無顛倒智，當知是名如來妙智。即於此中，若一切種智、若妙智，總合為一，名一切種妙智。如是一切，總名如來百四十種不共佛法。
items.en:
Second, explaining how the names arose; first, the Tathāgata's all-wisdom. Know that in this matter, the Tathāgatas' undistorted wisdom with respect to the heap leading towards the meaningless, and what leads towards neither the meaningful nor the meaningless, taken together, is called the Tathāgata's all-wisdom.
Second, the Tathāgata's wondrous wisdom. The Tathāgatas' undistorted wisdom with respect to the entire heap of dharmas leading towards the meaningful is called the Tathāgata's wondrous wisdom.
Third, wisdom of every kind. In this matter, taking all-wisdom and wondrous wisdom together as one is called wisdom of every kind.
Second, synthesising overall; first, concluding everything previously stated. All of this together is called the Tathāgata's own one hundred forty exclusive buddha-qualities.

items.zh: 即於此中，諸相、隨好，在菩薩位最後有中，皆已證得極善清淨。若時菩薩坐菩提座，住最後有，於菩薩道菩提資糧極善圓滿，爾時無師修三十七菩提分法，得

items.title: Section: The Supreme Transformation of Basis — Severing the Subtlest Trace of the Obstruction of the Knowable

items.zh: 一剎那名無障礙智三摩地，是其菩薩學道所攝金剛喻定。從此無間第二剎那，頓得其餘不共佛法。謂如來十力為初，一切種妙智為後，皆極清淨，悉為無上。由得此故，普於一切所知境界，無滯無障、最極清淨無垢智轉。依暫發悟思惟圓滿、意車圓滿，超過一切菩薩行、菩薩地，證入一切如來行、如來地。一切在肉所知障品所有麁重無餘斷故，得勝轉依。如是轉依最為無上。其餘一切乃至最上成滿住中菩薩轉依，當知有上。
items.en:
First, showing this attainment itself. Because every coarse hindrance of the obstruction of the knowable, lodged in the flesh, is severed without remainder, the supreme transformation of basis is attained.
Commentary: as for every coarse hindrance of the obstruction of the knowable lodged in the flesh — the Chapter on Abodes explains that the coarse hindrance of the obstruction of the knowable is itself of three kinds: coarse hindrance in the skin, coarse hindrance in the dermis, and coarse hindrance in the flesh. Know that the hindrance in the skin is entirely severed at the abode of utmost joy; the hindrance in the dermis is entirely severed at the abode of effortless, markless abiding; and the hindrance in the flesh is entirely severed only in the abode of the Tathāgata, yielding wisdom utterly pure of every obstruction.
Such a transformation of basis is the very highest, unsurpassed.
Second, distinguishing what remains. Every other transformation of basis, up to and including that of a bodhisattva abiding in the ground of ultimate accomplishment, should be understood as still having something higher to attain.

items.title: Section: Five Similes for the Gap Between a Tenth-Ground Bodhisattva and a Buddha's Own Wisdom

items.zh: 問：一切安住到究竟地菩薩智等、如來智等，云何應知此二差別？答：如明眼人隔於輕縠覩眾色像，一切安住到究竟地菩薩妙智於一切境，當知亦爾。如明眼人無所障隔覩眾色像，如來妙智於一切境，當知亦爾。如畫事業圓布眾彩，唯後妙色未淨修治，到究竟地菩薩妙智，當知亦爾。如畫事業圓布眾彩，最後妙色已淨修治，如來妙智，當知亦爾。如明眼人於微闇中覩見眾色，到究竟地菩薩妙智，當知亦爾。如明眼人離一切闇覩見眾色，如來妙智，當知亦爾。如明眼人遠覩眾色，到究竟地菩薩妙智，當知亦爾。如明眼人近覩眾色，如來妙智，當知亦爾。如輕瞖眼觀視眾色，到究竟地菩薩妙智，當知亦爾。如極淨眼觀視眾色，如來妙智，當知亦爾。
items.en:
Second, distinctions; first, posing the question. Question: for a bodhisattva abiding at the ultimate ground, and for the Tathāgata, how should this difference in wisdom and the rest be understood?
Second, answering; first, the distinction in wondrous wisdom; first, the simile of slight versus no obstruction; first, the bodhisattva. Answer: as a person of clear sight, viewing forms through a thin veil of gauze, so too should the wondrous wisdom of a bodhisattva abiding at the ultimate ground, with respect to every object, be understood.
Second, the Tathāgata. As a person of clear sight, viewing forms with no obstruction at all, so too should the Tathāgata's wondrous wisdom, with respect to every object, be understood.
Second, the simile of unpurified versus purified; first, the bodhisattva. As a painting fully covered in every colour, yet lacking the final, subtle colour not yet perfected, so too should the wondrous wisdom of a bodhisattva at the ultimate ground be understood.
Second, the Tathāgata. As a painting fully covered in every colour, its final, subtle colour already perfected, so too should the Tathāgata's wondrous wisdom be understood.
Third, the simile of faint darkness versus freedom from darkness; first, the bodhisattva. As a person of clear sight viewing forms in faint darkness, so too should the wondrous wisdom of a bodhisattva at the ultimate ground be understood.
Second, the Tathāgata. As a person of clear sight viewing forms entirely free of darkness, so too should the Tathāgata's wondrous wisdom be understood.
Fourth, the simile of viewing from afar versus viewing up close; first, the bodhisattva. As a person of clear sight viewing forms from afar, so too should the wondrous wisdom of a bodhisattva at the ultimate ground be understood.
Second, the Tathāgata. As a person of clear sight viewing forms up close, so too should the Tathāgata's wondrous wisdom be understood.
Fifth, the simile of a faintly clouded eye versus a perfectly clear eye; first, the bodhisattva. As an eye with faint cloudiness viewing forms, so too should the wondrous wisdom of a bodhisattva at the ultimate ground be understood.
Second, the Tathāgata. As a perfectly clear eye viewing forms, so too should the Tathāgata's wondrous wisdom be understood.

items.title: Section: Womb and Birth, and an Arhat's Dreaming Mind — Two Final Similes for Body and Mind

items.zh: 如處胎身，到究竟地諸菩薩身，當知亦爾。如出胎身，諸如來身，當知亦爾。如阿羅漢夢中心行，到究竟地菩薩心行，當知亦爾。
items.en:
Second, the distinction in body; first, the bodhisattva. As a body still within the womb, so too should the body of a bodhisattva at the ultimate ground be understood.
Second, the Tathāgata. As a body already born from the womb, so too should the body of every Tathāgata be understood.
Third, the distinction in mind; first, mental activity; first, the bodhisattva. As an arhat's mental activity while dreaming, so too should the mental activity of a bodhisattva at the ultimate ground be understood.

items.title: Section: A Lamp Dim and a Lamp Bright — Eight Similes Close, and the Buddha's Ten Great Deeds Begin

items.zh: 如阿羅漢覺時心行，如來心行，當知亦爾。如昧燈體、到究竟地菩薩智體，當知亦爾。如明燈體，如來智體，當知亦爾。是故當知，一切安住到究竟地諸菩薩眾，與諸如來妙智身心有大差別。如是如來證菩提已，遍於十方一切佛土，普能施作一切佛事。云何名為一切佛事？謂諸如來如來事業、如來所作，略有十種。如是一一如來事業、如來所作，能成無量利有情事。此外無有若過若增。
items.en:
Second, the Tathāgata. As an arhat's mental activity while fully awake, so too should the Tathāgata's mental activity be understood.
Second, the essence of wisdom; first, the bodhisattva. As the essence of a dim lamp, so too should the wisdom-essence of a bodhisattva at the ultimate ground be understood.
Second, the Tathāgata. As the essence of a bright lamp, so too should the Tathāgata's wisdom-essence be understood.
Third, concluding. Therefore know that between the assembly of bodhisattvas abiding at the ultimate ground and the Tathāgatas, there is a great difference in wondrous wisdom, body, and mind.
Third, buddha-deeds; first, stating. Thus, having realised awakening, the Tathāgata universally performs every buddha-deed throughout every buddha-land in every direction.
Second, posing the question. What are called all buddha-deeds?
Third, explaining; first, briefly stating ten kinds; first, stating. The Tathāgatas' own buddha-deeds, their own accomplishments, may briefly be said to be ten in number. Each single one of these accomplishes immeasurable benefit for beings; beyond this there is nothing excessive or additional.

items.title: Section: The First Three Buddha-Deeds — Inspiring Faith Through the Marks, Teaching Through Purity, Resolving Doubt Through the Powers

items.zh: 何等為十？謂諸如來最初自現大丈夫身，欲令有情心發淨信。大丈夫身於生淨信為最勝故，是名如來第一作事。如是作事，諸相、隨好所能成辦。又諸如來普為一切有情之類，起一切種教授加行，是名如來第二作事。如是作事，四一切種清淨所能成辦。又諸如來能作一切利有情事，能斷一切所生疑惑，是名如來第三作事。如是作事，如來十力所能成辦。由前所說如來十力，於能成辦一切有情一切義利有堪能故。又於如來所證十力所興問難，唯有如來能知、能見、能解、能了，唯有如來於彼問難能正答故。
items.en:
Second, posing the question. What are these ten?
Third, explaining; first, the first deed. The Tathāgatas first manifest their own great being's body, wishing beings' minds to arouse pure faith; since this is most excellent for generating pure faith, this is called the Tathāgata's first deed. This deed is accomplished through the marks and exemplary signs.
Second, the second deed. The Tathāgatas universally arouse every kind of instructive effort for every kind of being; this is called the Tathāgata's second deed. This deed is accomplished through the four kinds of utter purity.
Third, the third deed; first, stating. The Tathāgatas accomplish every deed benefiting beings and sever every doubt that arises; this is called the Tathāgata's third deed. This deed is accomplished through the ten powers.
Second, explaining; first, accomplishing benefit. Because the ten powers already explained have the capacity to accomplish every benefit for every being.
Second, resolving questions. Also, regarding whatever questions arise concerning what the Tathāgata has realised through the ten powers, only the Tathāgata can know, see, understand, and correctly answer them.

blocks.text: The list of a buddha's hundred and forty qualities ends. Then a series of similes for the last, smallest gap between a tenth-ground bodhisattva and a buddha.

Undistorted wisdom about the unwholesome and neutral is "all-wisdom"; about the wholesome, "wondrous wisdom". Master Cháng Bǎi: none of these qualities is shared with the two vehicles, nor even with bodhisattvas, who only partly resemble them.

In the bodhisattva's final existence the marks and signs are fully purified. Seated on the seat of awakening, with the provisions complete, the bodhisattva cultivates the thirty-seven factors without a teacher and attains awakening.

subs.head: The supreme transformation of the basis

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng: the skin-level impediments are the discriminated grasping of dharmas; those beneath the skin are innate grasping, cut at the eighth ground. Master Cháng Bǎi: the flesh-level is the subtlest, cut without remainder (Day 431). The ripening consciousness becomes stainless consciousness and the great mirror wisdom.

Seeing through fine gauze versus seeing without obstruction. Venerable Miào Jìng: a fine gauze, still a little unclear. Master Cháng Bǎi: a painting where only the last fine stroke of colour remains unfinished.
Venerable Miào Jìng: dreaming or not, the arhat's mind is pure. Master Cháng Bǎi: yet waking is purer still.

Showing the great being's body to arouse pure faith. Master Cháng Bǎi: beings cling to form, so this is most powerful. Declaration shows beings their own good and bad conduct; instruction teaches the foundations of mindfulness and the severing of affliction.
"Only the last fine stroke remains." The tenth-ground bodhisattva is almost a buddha, and the treatise still marks the difference.

quiz.q: How are all-wisdom and wondrous wisdom distinguished?
options: the first regards the meaningless and neutral heaps; the second the meaningful heap
quiz.why: Undistorted wisdom about the unwholesome and neutral is all-wisdom; about the wholesome is wondrous wisdom.

quiz.q: Why are the hundred and forty qualities called "unshared," per the lectures?
options: only buddhas complete them; not shared with the two vehicles or fully with bodhisattvas
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: not shared with the two vehicles, nor with bodhisattvas, who only partly resemble them. Venerable Miào Jìng: only the Buddha is complete in these.

quiz.q: How do the lectures assign the skin, dermis, and flesh hindrances?
options: skin: discriminated grasping; dermis: innate grasping cut at the eighth ground; flesh: subtlest, cut only at buddhahood
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: skin-level is discriminated grasping of dharmas; dermis-level innate grasping, cut at the eighth ground. Master Cháng Bǎi: flesh-level is the subtlest, cut without remainder.

quiz.q: In the supreme transformation of basis, what is transformed?
options: the ripening store consciousness becomes stainless consciousness, the great mirror wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the ripening consciousness becomes stainless consciousness and the great mirror wisdom. Venerable Miào Jìng: the store consciousness becomes stainless; the mind is then pure.

quiz.q: Which simile contrasts the bodhisattva's and the Tathāgata's seeing?
options: seeing through thin gauze and seeing with nothing between
quiz.why: Seeing through gauze versus unobstructed. Venerable Miào Jìng: a fine gauze, still a little unclear.

quiz.q: "A painting lacking the final colour." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: only the last subtle stroke remains — nearly complete
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: only the last fine stroke of colour remains unfinished.

quiz.q: How do the lectures explain the arhat's dreaming versus waking mind?
options: even dreaming he is pure, but waking is purer; so too buddha and bodhisattva
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: dreaming or not, the arhat's mind is pure. Master Cháng Bǎi: yet waking is purer still.

quiz.q: What is the first deed, and what accomplishes it?
options: showing the great being's body to arouse faith; the marks and signs
quiz.why: Showing the great being's body to arouse pure faith, accomplished through the marks and signs. Master Cháng Bǎi: beings cling to form, so this is most powerful.

quiz.q: The second deed is instruction. Which miraculous transformations does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: the transformation of declaration shows one's mental conduct; of instruction teaches the foundations of mindfulness and severing affliction
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: declaration shows beings their own good and bad conduct; instruction teaches the foundations of mindfulness and severing affliction.
